scope: Wire the already approved 2-DIP keyboard focus outline into the Candidate Dock; no new design values, colours, shortcuts or semantics.
before_mismatch: the candidate-rail container drew a 1-DIP border_1 and used its colour to mean keyboard focus
dock rows drew border_1 and reused the focus colour for the active row while the dock was focused, so focus, selection and the structural separator were the same 1-DIP border
the container focus handle never receives keyboard focus directly (tab lands on dock rows), so a container-only ring would never light in a real session

implementation.focus_indicator: one ring on the focusable Candidate Dock container at the approved focus_outline width, lit when the dock handle or any descendant row holds keyboard focus
implementation.why_constant_width: GPUI draws borders inside the box and has no outline primitive; a constant ring width means acquiring focus changes colour only and never layout, hit target or scroll geometry
implementation.structural_separator: dock row borders use shell_style::separator (exactly one physical pixel at any scale factor) and draw nothing when the scale factor is unusable
implementation.selection: row colour depends on selection only (DOCK_SELECTED_COLOR) and never on keyboard focus, so the two states stay distinguishable
implementation.token_source: shell_style::focus_outline -> DesignTokens.geometry.focus_outline_dip (FOCUS_OUTLINE_DIP = 2.0), no new width constant

coverage_map.T01: ring width equals focus_outline(2.0) and the override value
coverage_map.T02: ring colour differs when unfocused; rows never draw the focus colour
coverage_map.T03: row colour is selection-only, so a selected unfocused row shows no focus colour
coverage_map.T04: selection and focus are separate inputs to separate painters
coverage_map.T06: row border is one physical pixel at 1.0/1.25/1.5/2.0

quality.result: all quality gates passed (native smoke separate)
